topic: live-voice comparison round 2026-10-26: zero coefficients vs the retired stale model
question: with the speaker at 100 cm side-facing and the metal plate damped, can a listener hear intelligible amplification at a gain that does not regenerate?

config.coefficients: zero (candidate model loaded with zero_coeff=True); the stale model_room_side_512.json was retired to ...STALE-oldfixture.json
config.listener: 20 cm from the speaker, about 100 cm from the source

runs.listener: amplification audible, but not clear; a white-noise-like layer covers the voice after the first moment
no audible amplification except a clear burst at the start; white-noise masking
cannot hear the human voice at all

runs.note: intended as a 5 cm close-talk point but the microphone level moved only +0.7 dB, so the speech almost certainly missed the capture window; this run is INVALID and no conclusion is drawn from it

finding.negative_but_bounded: -6 dB regenerates enough to mask speech (mode share 0.37-0.70); -8 dB is clean (0.12) but the amplified voice is inaudible
finding.first_positive_observation: at -6 dB the listener did hear amplification for the first time in this project; the problem is masking by near-regeneration, not absence of gain

premise_checks_still_open: close-talk at 5 cm was not actually exercised: the microphone level barely moved, so the speech timing missed the 0.336 s capture window. This is the only remaining lever that raises the output without raising loop gain and it has NOT been tested.
a high-pass or low-frequency suppression around 465 Hz could remove the masking rumble; this requires coefficients, i.e. B's matching model or an explicit high-pass design
not_claimed: no claim that the hardware is at its limit
no claim that no configuration works
